f4.quote: Increasing Ta-Nb-V changed the alloy from single HCP HZTX0 through a BCC-dominant state containing residual HCP and, at low addition (especially HZTX0.1), abundant hard and brittle omega phase, toward an essentially single-BCC structure at high x.

f5.quote: At x = 0.1, omega-phase precipitation causes brittle fracture and extensive fragmentation.

f6.quote: Ta, Nb, and V act as beta/BCC stabilizers, lowering BCC free energy and suppressing HCP and omega formation at sufficient concentration.

f7.quote: At larger x, atomic-size and modulus mismatch produces lattice distortion and solute-dislocation interactions that impede glide, providing solid-solution strengthening

f8.quote: Fragmentation exposes reactive Hf and Zr to atmospheric oxygen, causing rapid exothermic oxidation and visible sparks

f9.quote: HZTX0.1 composition instead was expected to be brittle but to release energy most rapidly and intensely because it fragments most completely.

f10.quote: HZTX0.9 was identified as the best reported balance: higher strength and ductility than the base alloy
